title: Passwords.
description: A deliberately silly password generator that turns a functional utility into a small, characterful experience.

sections.title: What it is
text: An installable web app that generates 'passwords' made with bad words, insults, and more. Including sound effects, small interactions, and irreverent commentary.
It is designed as an entertaining experiment, not as a secure source of passwords for important accounts or services.

sections.title: What it demonstrates
text: The project explores how interaction, tone, and feedback can make a familiar utility feel distinctive. It can be installed and used offline.

sections.title: Built with
text: SvelteKit, the Web Audio API, and Cloudflare.

title: Panorama Tab
description: A customizable browser new-tab page designed to not get in the way, with a basic summary of the day for your current location and customizable backgrounds.

sections.title: Project background
text: I have developed this long-running browser-extension project over time as both a product and a space to explore design and development.
It replaces the default new-tab page with a daily overview, including the date, local time, weather, and a personal greeting.

sections.title: Design approach
text: People can personalize the background with photography, colors, or gradients. The experience is designed to stay simple and private: settings remain on the device, and there is no account or premium tier.

sections.title: The result
text: Panorama Tab brings product thinking, visual design, and front-end development together in a product that continues to evolve.

title: Domain Register
description: A mobile domain-management experience designed to make common registrar tasks easier to handle away from a desktop.

sections.title: The challenge
text: Managing domains on a phone can mean switching to a desktop for tasks such as searching for domains, managing DNS, renewing registrations, or exploring add-on services.

sections.title: What I designed
text: I designed a native mobile app concept that brings key domain tasks into one place, including domain search, transfers, renewals, DNS management, and an overview of registered domains.
The design also considers practical mobile details such as quick access to common actions, biometric authentication, notifications, and access to domain information offline.

sections.title: What it demonstrates
text: This project explores how to organize a broad set of account and domain-management tasks into a clear mobile experience.

title: Stoop Inbox
description: A redesign concept for a newsletter app, focused on making subscriptions easier to organize and articles more enjoyable to read.

sections.title: The challenge
text: The existing experience made some useful actions difficult to find and presented repeated controls across the app. Organizing subscriptions and adjusting notifications also needed more attention.

sections.title: What I redesigned
text: I reorganized the experience around the inbox, a library for saved and unfinished reading, newsletter discovery, and a focused reading view.
The concept also includes controls for reading appearance, organization, and notification preferences.

sections.title: What it demonstrates
text: This project shows how research into an existing product and its user feedback can inform a clearer information architecture and a more cohesive reading experience.

title: Timesets
description: A simple app to create your own Pomodoro-like timers to keep track of your tasks.

sections.title: Project background
text: Customizable focus timers inspired by the Pomodoro technique.
